name: Connecting Ridge
note: Ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters; the best-lit point near the pole (Gläser et al. 2014). NASA names the Shackleton connecting ridge as the destination of Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mark 1 pathfinder with NASA payloads, planned for 2027.

name: Peak near Shackleton
note: A peak with long sunlight about 15 km outside the rim of Shackleton crater. The area is the widely reported target of China's planned Chang'e-7 mission (location approximate).

name: Malapert Massif
note: 5-km-high mountain that faces Earth; one of NASA's nine candidate regions for the first Artemis crewed landing. NASA publishes an outline for this region, not a point. This is the best-lit spot inside the outline on NASA's average illumination map.

name: Mons Mouton (IM-2)
note: Intuitive Machines IM-2 'Athena' landed here on 6 Mar 2025, tipped over and lost power within a day. The point lies inside NASA's Mons Mouton Plateau candidate region.

name: Malapert A (IM-1)
note: Intuitive Machines IM-1 'Odysseus', the first commercial Moon landing (22 Feb 2024).

name: Shiv Shakti (Chandrayaan-3)
note: India's Chandrayaan-3 landed here on 23 Aug 2023 — the closest landing to the south pole at the time.

name: Nobile region (Griffin-1)
note: Astrobotic's Griffin Mission 1 (CLPS, not yet launched) is aimed at the area near Nobile crater. Point approximate: the site once chosen for NASA's VIPER rover. It lies inside NASA's Mons Mouton candidate region.

name: de Gerlache Rim 2
note: Rim of de Gerlache crater, one of NASA's nine Artemis candidate regions. NASA publishes an outline for this region, not a point. This is the best-lit spot inside the outline on NASA's average illumination map.

name: Haworth
note: Highland by Haworth crater, one of NASA's nine Artemis candidate regions. NASA publishes an outline for this region, not a point. This is the best-lit spot inside the outline on NASA's average illumination map.

name: Nobile Rim 1
note: Rim of Nobile crater on the flank of Mons Mouton, one of NASA's nine Artemis candidate regions. NASA publishes an outline for this region, not a point. This is the best-lit spot inside the outline on NASA's average illumination map.

name: Nobile Rim 2
note: A second stretch of the Nobile rim, one of NASA's nine Artemis candidate regions. NASA publishes an outline for this region, not a point. This is the best-lit spot inside the outline on NASA's average illumination map.

name: Mons Mouton Plateau
note: Broad flat top of Mons Mouton, the largest of NASA's nine Artemis candidate regions. NASA publishes an outline for this region, not a point. This is the best-lit spot inside the outline on NASA's average illumination map.

name: Mons Mouton
note: Slope of Mons Mouton, the highest mountain near the pole and one of NASA's nine Artemis candidate regions. NASA publishes an outline for this region, not a point. This is the best-lit spot inside the outline on NASA's average illumination map.

name: Slater Plain
note: Plain beside Slater crater, one of NASA's nine Artemis candidate regions. NASA publishes an outline for this region, not a point. This is the best-lit spot inside the outline on NASA's average illumination map.

name: Peak near Cabeus B
note: High ground by Cabeus B crater, one of NASA's nine Artemis candidate regions. NASA publishes an outline for this region, not a point. This is the best-lit spot inside the outline on NASA's average illumination map.

name: Mare Crisium (Blue Ghost M1)
note: Firefly's Blue Ghost Mission 1 landed here on 2 Mar 2025 and worked for a full lunar day. Far from the poles; shown with a smooth horizon.

name: Apollo basin (Chang'e-6)
note: China's Chang'e-6 landed on the far side on 1 Jun 2024 and returned samples. Earth is never in the sky here, so every message needs a relay satellite. Shown with a smooth horizon.

name: Apollo 11
note: Mare Tranquillitatis near the equator: the Sun climbs high and the horizon is flat. Shown for contrast with the pole.
